frictionSummary: Connected App setup is self-serve inside an org; AppExchange distribution adds an optional security review.
prerequisites: A Salesforce org (a free Developer Edition org works) with System Administrator access
Salesforce is steering new integrations toward External Client Apps (ECA) rather than the older Connected App type — check which your target org expects
A callback URL you control, for the Authorization Code (with PKCE) flow

steps.title: Create a Connected App (or External Client App)
steps.body: Setup → App Manager → New Connected App (or New External Client App on orgs where ECA is available). Enable OAuth Settings.

steps.title: Set the callback URL and OAuth scopes
steps.body: Enter your callback URL and select the OAuth scopes your integration needs. For ECAs, PKCE and refresh-token security controls live under the app's Security settings — leaving "Require Secret for Refresh Token Flow" misconfigured is a common cause of token refresh failures.

steps.title: Retrieve the Consumer Key and Secret
steps.body: After saving, Salesforce generates a Consumer Key (client ID) and Consumer Secret. These can take a few minutes to activate on a new org.
steps.codeSnippet:
curl -X POST https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CONSUMER_KEY \
  -d client_secret=YOUR_CONSUMER_SECRET \
  -d redirect_uri=YOUR_CALLBACK_URL \
  -d code=THE_AUTH_CODE

steps.title: If distributing via AppExchange, submit for Security Review
steps.body: Listing a packaged app on AppExchange requires passing Salesforce's ISV Security Review — a formal, multi-week process distinct from basic Connected App setup, which itself needs no review.

scopes.grants: Access and manage the user's Salesforce data via the API
Obtain a refresh token for offline/long-lived access

approval.expectedWait: None for internal Connected App use within your own org; multi-week ISV Security Review only for AppExchange listing
approval.notes: Doc-sourced. Creating and using a Connected App inside your own org requires no review. Only packaging and distributing via the AppExchange marketplace triggers Salesforce's formal ISV Security Review.

gotchas: Salesforce is migrating new integrations toward External Client Apps (ECA); older Connected Apps still work but new security controls (PKCE, refresh-token rotation, IP restrictions) are documented primarily for ECAs
A newly created Consumer Key/Secret can take several minutes to propagate before the first OAuth request succeeds
For ECAs, an unchecked "Require Secret for Refresh Token Flow" setting is a common, non-obvious cause of refresh failures
AppExchange's ISV Security Review is a distinct, multi-week process — don't assume it's required just to use OAuth inside your own org

do: Install jsforce (Node) or simple-salesforce (Python) for the OAuth + API flow
Add placeholder env vars: SALESFORCE_CLIENT_ID, SALESFORCE_CLIENT_SECRET, SALESFORCE_REDIRECT_URI
Wire up a "Connect Salesforce" button redirecting to https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/authorize with response_type=code
Use PKCE if the developer's app is set up as an External Client App
dont: Create the Connected App / External Client App in the org, or submit for ISV Security Review — those are the developer's call
Enter the real Consumer Secret anywhere — leave it as an env placeholder
Assume login.salesforce.com is always correct — sandboxes use test.salesforce.com
